findings.claim_broken: Evidence Limit 7: 'one runner of several dying shows as failures, not as 503'. Measured: it shows as nothing. loop.failures is only populated when WorkerLoop.run's gather returns (loop.py:113-116), i.e. after the LAST runner ends, so a partly dead pool reports readyz 200 / failures 0 / livez 200 for its whole life. A runner dies permanently on any non-DomainError from claim_candidate, jobs.claim or load_work (a transient Valkey/PostgreSQL blip; _runner has no try), the process never exits, the unit's Restart=always never fires, and the pilot's single worker silently runs at reduced concurrency until the last runner dies.
findings.evidence: Probe P6 (concurrency=2, first claim_candidate raises ConnectionError once): {dead_runners: 1, readyz: [200, failures=0, ready=True], livez: [200, True], surviving_runner_completed: True, failures_after_stop: 1}. No case in tests/w/test_service.py exercises a partly dead pool; my mutants R14/R16 (drain/serve behaviour on a dead pool) survived.
findings.minimal_fix: In readiness(): dead = sum(1 for t in self.loop._tasks if t.done() and not t.cancelled() and t.exception() is not None); report it as 'runners_dead' and make 'live' false when dead > 0 (or end serve() when any runner task completes: asyncio.wait({waiting, *self.loop._tasks}, FIRST_COMPLETED)), so the unit restarts to full concurrency; add a case that kills one of two runners and asserts 503 on /livez. Root cause is W2's _runner not surviving a transient claim error; note it as a W follow-up and correct Limit 7.

findings.claim_broken: Two stated readiness invariants have no killable test: (a) 'an engine slower than 2 s to say ready is not ready' - mutant R4 (asyncio.timeout(None)) survived; no case has a hanging health(). (b) 'never public' is proven only at construction: mutant R13 (start_server bound to 0.0.0.0 regardless of health_host) survived because every case connects via 127.0.0.1, which a 0.0.0.0 listener also answers; and health_host is a plain mutable dataclass field, so `service.health_host = '0.0.0.0'` after construction binds publicly (probe P8b: getsockname() == ('0.0.0.0', 41611)).

(b) move the loopback check into a helper called from both __post_init__ and start(), and in the PUBLIC case assert service._server.sockets[0].getsockname()[0] == '127.0.0.1'.

findings.minimal_fix: Bind the listener first (or before reap_once), then create the pool and reaper tasks; a case that pre-binds the port and asserts no candidate was claimed.
